During the term and the Exit Period, the Supplier shall keep records for the periods in [Schedule [ ] (Retention Periods)], or longer where the Bank instructs, and shall then return and delete them under [the exit clause]. It shall test the retrieval procedure with the Bank [at least annually] and report the results.
watchFor: **Retrieval as a change request:** exports or retrieval available only through the change-control procedure, at professional-services rates or 'subject to capacity'. Regulatory requests should not wait (see the change-control clause).
**Proprietary formats:** data available only through the Supplier's console, in a proprietary format with no documented schema, or as backups encrypted under keys only the Supplier holds.

**Suspension and deletion:** a right to suspend platform access for non-payment, or to delete data a fixed period after termination whether or not the Bank has its copy (see the termination clause on exit and data return).
**Short retention:** logs and records kept only for the Supplier's standard period, such as 90 days, below what the Bank needs. AMLO record periods are dealt with in the AML vendor clause.

pushback.says: You can reach everything through our console, so local copies are unnecessary.
pushback.reply: The console is fine as one route. But a digital bank must keep a full set of books and records accessible to the MA (Digital Bank Guideline para 13), and must produce them to an examiner on demand (BO s.56). That cannot depend on your platform being up or our account being in good standing. This is a must-have.

pushback.says: We cannot commit to 24-hour retrieval for regulatory requests.
pushback.reply: The figure is negotiable; prompt retrieval is not. Our books and records must stay accessible to the MA (Digital Bank Guideline para 13), and CDD and transaction records must be available swiftly to the HKMA and auditors (AML Guideline 8.2(b)). Most requests will be met from our own daily copy, so this covers only the rest. A tested self-service export with an assistance commitment can justify a longer turnaround for archived records.

pushback.says: Suspending access for non-payment is our standard remedy.
pushback.reply: Pursue payment by other means. Cutting off our records could expose our directors, chief executive and managers to an offence under BO s.56(2), so access to records cannot be suspended for any reason.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Legal with the CRO and the CFO, who owns the books and accounts; if the Supplier will not accept the red lines, take it to the outsourcing committee before proceeding.

terms.title: Confidentiality of all customer information
terms.summary: The bank's common-law duty of confidentiality covers corporate as well as individual customers (SA-2 footnote 1), and SA-2 2.5.2 asks for safeguards for customer information generally. The confidentiality clause should therefore reach all customer information, not only personal data (drafting conclusion).
require: **Undertakings:** SA-2 expects controls and proper safeguards for customer information, and lists as typical safeguards (examples, not a mandatory list) undertakings by the vendor that it and its staff will abide by confidentiality rules, including taking account of the PDPO data protection principles (2.5.2).
**Remedies:** another typical safeguard in 2.5.2 is a contractual right for the bank to take action against the vendor for a breach of confidentiality.

**Staff and agents (technology outsourcing):** the agreement should specify the provider's performance standards and other obligations (TM-G-1 7.1.1); footnote 13 says these 'may include' keeping confidential the bank's information obtained by the provider's staff or agents, and complying with the bank's relevant IT control policies and procedures.

sources.label: SPM SA-2 Outsourcing
sources.note: Footnote 1 to 2.5.1: the common-law duty covers individual and corporate customers alike, while the PDPO protects only individuals; the general principle is that customer data is kept confidential and not divulged to anyone without the customer's consent.

sources.label: Digital Bank Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.16(10) of the Banking Ordinance, not s.7(3). The MA must be satisfied that confidentiality and integrity of customer information will not be compromised, and that the PDPO and common-law customer confidentiality are complied with (para 23).

sources.label: Code of Banking Practice (Dec 2023)
sources.note: Banks should treat customers' (and former customers') banking affairs as private and confidential. Non-statutory, but the HKMA expects compliance and monitors it (CoBP 1.2, 1.4).

drafting: **Definition:** define confidential information to include all customer information and the bank's own information, and keep the obligation alive after termination; the Code's recommendation extends to former customers (8.1).
**Compelled disclosure:** allow disclosure required by law only after prompt notice to the bank, so far as the law permits.

playbook.why: The MA must be satisfied that outsourcing will not compromise the confidentiality of customer information and that common-law customer confidentiality is complied with (Digital Bank Guideline para 23, a statutory guideline under BO s.16(10)). The SA-2 2.5.2 undertakings and remedies are expected safeguards that deliver it.
preferred: **All customer information:** The clause covers all Bank Data and other Bank information, for corporate and individual customers, current and former, whether or not marked, without time limit for customer information (SA-2 footnote 1; CoBP 8.1).
**Use only for the Services:** The Supplier may use confidential information only to perform the Services, with no residuals, benchmarking or aggregated-data rights over Customer Data.
**People bound:** Personnel and Subcontractors with access are bound in writing, and the Supplier answers for them as for itself (SA-2 2.5.2; TM-G-1 7.1.1, footnote 13).

**Real remedies:** An express right to act for breach, including injunctive relief (SA-2 2.5.2). The Bank stays accountable to customers for the Supplier's breaches (CoBP 8.8), so confidentiality losses should sit outside the general cap (counsel's drafting; see the liability clause).
fallback: **Mutual clause:** Accept a mutual confidentiality clause, only if Customer Data gets the full protection and the usual exceptions (prior knowledge, independent development, receipt from a third party) do not apply to it.

**Fixed term for business information:** Accept a survival period of [5] years for the Bank's non-customer business information, only if the obligations for customer information continue without time limit.

**Equivalent terms:** Accept the Supplier's employment-contract terms for its staff, or a hosting Subcontractor's standard confidentiality terms, instead of back-to-back undertakings, only if they cover Bank information and bar own-purpose use, staff are trained on them, and the Supplier stays liable for breaches.

**Notice after the event:** Where the law bars advance notice of a compelled disclosure, accept notice as soon as the law allows and disclosure of the minimum required. See the overseas authorities clause for foreign requests.
redLines: **Scope floor:** No clause limited to personal data or to marked information that leaves any customer information, individual or corporate, unprotected (Digital Bank Guideline para 23; SA-2 footnote 1). Protection of the Bank's other information can be traded (see fallback).

**Everyone with access bound:** No signature unless every person the Supplier lets see customer information is bound and the Supplier answers for them; otherwise confidentiality can be compromised through them (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

**Regulator not blocked:** No term restricting disclosure to the Regulator or the Bank's auditors, or making it subject to Supplier consent (Digital Bank Guideline para 23; SA-2 2.8.2). See the HKMA access clause.
model: (a) The Supplier shall keep confidential all Bank Data and all other information relating to the Bank, its group or its current or former customers, whether individuals or corporations, that the Supplier or any Subcontractor obtains in connection with this Agreement or its negotiation, before or after its date, whether or not marked confidential (together, "Confidential Information"). The Supplier shall use Confidential Information only to perform the Services.

(b) The Supplier shall disclose Confidential Information only to its personnel and Subcontractors who need it to perform the Services and are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than this clause and, excluding Customer Data, to its professional advisers bound by a duty of confidence. The Supplier is liable for every act or omission of those persons in relation to Confidential Information as if it were its own.

(c) Nothing in this Agreement restricts any disclosure of information to the Regulator, or any disclosure by the Bank to its auditors, professional advisers or members of its group or as Applicable Law requires of the Bank. None of those disclosures requires the Supplier's consent. Any other disclosure that the Supplier or a Subcontractor is legally compelled to make is governed by paragraph (d).

(d) If any law, court order or authority other than the Regulator requires the Supplier or a Subcontractor to disclose Confidential Information, the Supplier shall, so far as the law permits, notify the Bank [promptly and before disclosure], cooperate with any lawful step the Bank takes to resist or limit the disclosure, and disclose only the minimum required. For an Overseas Authority Request, clause [Overseas authorities] also applies and prevails.

(e) Paragraph (a) does not apply to information, other than Customer Data, that is or becomes public other than through a breach of this Agreement, or that the Supplier shows by written records it lawfully held free of any duty of confidence before receiving it in connection with this Agreement.

(f) Any actual or suspected unauthorised disclosure of Confidential Information is an Incident to be notified under clause [Incidents]. Damages alone may not be an adequate remedy for a breach of this clause, and the Bank may seek injunctive relief or specific performance. This clause survives termination or expiry of this Agreement without limit of time.
watchFor: **Narrow definition:** confidential information limited to material 'marked or identified as confidential', or to personal data only, so corporate customer information falls outside.
**Residuals and aggregates:** a right to use information kept in staff's unaided memory, or 'aggregated' or 'de-identified' customer information, for the Supplier's own products or benchmarking.
**Sunset:** all obligations ending [2] or [3] years after termination, including those for customer information.

**Cap that swallows the clause:** confidentiality and data breaches left inside a general cap of [12] months' charges, or excluded as 'loss of data' or 'indirect loss', so customer remediation, notification and Incident costs cannot be recovered. See the liability clause.

pushback.says: Our standard mutual NDA covers this.
pushback.reply: We can use a mutual form, but it must cover all customer information, corporate as well as individual, marked or not. The MA must be satisfied that confidentiality of customer information will not be compromised (Digital Bank Guideline para 23), so this is a must-have.

pushback.says: We cannot accept confidentiality without an end date.
pushback.reply: For our business information we can agree a fixed period. Customer information is different: our duty to customers does not lapse when your contract ends, and the Code extends it to former customers (CoBP 8.1).

pushback.says: We cannot accept unlimited liability for confidentiality or data breaches.
pushback.reply: We can discuss a separate, higher cap for confidentiality and data breaches, but not the general cap, and it must cover customer remediation, notification and incident response costs. We stay accountable to customers for your breaches (CoBP 8.8), so our right to act against you (SA-2 2.5.2) must be worth something. See the liability clause.

playbook.escalate: Suggested: Head of Legal for any change to the definition, survival or Regulator carve-out, with the CRO (and the Data Protection Officer where Personal Data is involved) before signing anything that misses a red line.

terms.title: Personal data processing (PDPO)
terms.summary: This is the main place where statute itself requires the bank to control a vendor (the other statutory hooks are narrower: AMLO Sch. 2 s.18 for CDD intermediaries, and Cap. 653 for a designated CI operator). Whenever the bank engages a data processor, in or outside Hong Kong, it must adopt contractual or other means to stop the processor keeping the data longer than necessary for processing and to protect it against unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use. For an external vendor, a contract is the practical means.
require: **Retention (DPP2(3)):** prevent personal data transferred to the processor being kept longer than necessary for processing it.
**Security (DPP4(2)):** prevent unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use of the data transferred for processing.

**Purpose:** the bank controls the data and remains the data user. DPP3 therefore still governs what the vendor may be asked to do: without the data subject's prescribed consent (express, voluntary and not withdrawn in writing), the data may not be used for a new purpose (DPP3; s.2(3)). The Code assumes the processing purposes are stated in the outsourcing agreement and measures retention against them (CoBP 8.8), so state them there.

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: Contractual or other means against over-retention by a data processor.

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: Contractual or other means against unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use.

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: On or before collection, the data subject must be explicitly informed of the classes of persons to whom the data may be transferred. Naming data processors as a class in the collection notice applies this (inference).

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: An act done by a person as the bank's agent, with its express or implied authority, is treated as done by the bank as well. This applies only where the vendor is in law the bank's agent, and not in criminal proceedings (s.65(4)).

sources.label: SPM SA-2 Outsourcing
sources.note: The arrangement should comply with the PDPO and the common-law duty of confidentiality; this generally involves legal advice.

sources.label: Code of Banking Practice (Dec 2023)
sources.note: Satisfy yourself first that the provider will keep the data confidential and safe; use contractual or other means against misuse and over-retention, tied to the purposes in the outsourcing agreement; stay accountable to customers. Notify customers on or before collection, as specifically as possible, that their data may go to data processors (8.3(b)).

drafting: **Processor role (drafting point; the PDPO defines the term but does not require this clause):** confine the vendor to processing on the bank's behalf and not for any of its own purposes. That matches the DPP2(4) definition of 'data processor', and under s.2(12) such a vendor is not itself a data user. A vendor that also uses the data for its own purposes is outside the definition, and passing it the data is a 'use' that must satisfy DPP3.

**Consequences:** breach of a data protection principle is not itself an offence (s.64A(2)(a)). After an investigation, however, the Privacy Commissioner can serve an enforcement notice (s.50), and contravening it is an offence (s.50A). An individual customer who suffers damage, including injury to feelings, can claim compensation from the bank as data user, subject to a defence of having taken reasonable care (s.66). Corporate customers have no PDPO claim; their protection is the common-law duty of confidentiality.
**'Other means':** the statute allows contractual or other means, but for an external vendor a contract is the practical way to show compliance.

**Usual terms:** instructions-only processing, security measures, no other use or disclosure, controls on sub-processing, prompt breach notification, return or erasure at the end, and audit rights. The security detail sits in the information security clause; sub-processing, breach notification and audit have their own clauses.
terms.cloud: Cloud and SaaS providers usually present themselves as processors and offer a data-processing addendum (a practice observation, not from the sources). Check that it gives the bank contractual means meeting both DPP2(3) and DPP4(2), and that the provider reserves no right to use the data for its own purposes, such as product improvement or analytics; if it does, it is not a 'data processor' under DPP2(4).

playbook.why: Whenever the bank engages a data processor, in or outside Hong Kong, the PDPO requires it to adopt contractual or other means against over-retention and against unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use (DPP2(3), DPP4(2)). This is statute, and for an external vendor the contract is the practical means.
preferred: **Processor only:** The Supplier processes Personal Data only on the Bank's documented instructions and for the purposes stated in the agreement, never for its own purposes (DPP2(4); s.2(12); CoBP 8.8).
**Retention timetable:** Return or erasure on a fixed timetable when each purpose ends and at exit, covering Subcontractor copies and backups, with written certification (DPP2(3)).
**Security by cross-reference:** The DPP4(2) means are delivered through the information security and segregation clauses, scaled to the kind of data and the harm that could result (DPP4(1)(a)).

**Help with requests:** Prompt assistance with data access and correction requests, complaints and Privacy Commissioner enquiries, so the Bank can meet the 40-day deadline for data access requests (s.19(1)).
fallback: **Supplier's addendum:** Accept the Supplier's data processing addendum, only if it meets DPP2(3) and DPP4(2), gives the Supplier no own-purpose use, and yields to the Bank's terms on conflict. Keep the gap analysis on file.
**Backup cycle:** Accept erasure from backups on the normal rotation, only if a maximum period is stated (for example [90] days), the backups stay protected, and they are restored only for the Bank.

**'Other means':** Where the Supplier cannot read the data, for example under encryption with keys only the Bank holds, accept that technical control as part of the DPP4(2) means. Means against over-retention are still needed; they are usually contract terms, unless the Bank itself controls deletion (DPP2(3)).

**Legal hold:** Accept retention that law binding the Supplier requires, only if the Supplier names the law and the data, keeps it protected under this Agreement, uses it for nothing else and erases it when the requirement ends. The Data Protection Officer should confirm DPP2(3) is met.
redLines: **Retention means:** No signature without contractual or other means ensuring that Personal Data is not kept longer than necessary for processing, with return or erasure at the end (PDPO DPP2(3)). For an external vendor, this is normally an enforceable contract term.
**Security means:** No signature without contractual or other means against unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use of the data transferred (PDPO DPP4(2)).

**No own-purpose use:** No Supplier right to use Customer Data or other Personal Data processed for the Services for its own purposes, except Bank staff contact details used only to run the account (counsel's drafting). It would not then be a data processor, and a new purpose needs prescribed consent (DPP2(4), DPP3).
model: (a) The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the Bank's behalf, for the purposes in [Schedule [ ] (Processing)] and on the Bank's documented instructions, and not for its own or any third party's purposes, including analytics, benchmarking, product development or the training of any model. It may use business contact details of Bank personnel only to administer this Agreement. Clause [Sub-contracting] applies to any Subcontractor that processes Personal Data.

(b) The Supplier shall not keep Personal Data longer than necessary to perform the Services. Within [30] days after a purpose in [Schedule [ ] (Processing)] ends, or on the Bank's instruction, it shall return or erase the relevant Personal Data, including Subcontractor copies, as the Bank directs, and certify this in writing. On termination or expiry, erasure starts only after the Exit Period, once the Bank confirms it holds a complete copy.

(c) Backup copies of Personal Data may be kept only until overwritten in the Supplier's normal backup cycle, which shall not exceed [90] days. Until then they remain subject to this Agreement and shall be restored only for the Bank.

(d) The Supplier shall protect Personal Data against unauthorized or accidental access, processing, erasure, loss or use by maintaining at least the measures in clause [Information security] and clause [Segregation and access], and any further measures appropriate to the kind of Personal Data and the harm that could result from its misuse.

(e) The Supplier shall refer to the Bank [within [2] Business Days] any data access or correction request, or complaint, from a data subject, and respond only as the Bank instructs. Within [5] Business Days of the Bank's request, it shall give the Bank the information and help it needs to handle any such matter, or to inform the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data or data subjects of an Incident affecting Personal Data.

(f) So far as the law permits, the Supplier shall promptly tell the Bank of any enquiry from the Commissioner about Personal Data; nothing in this Agreement restricts it from complying with the Commissioner's lawful requirements. It shall promptly tell the Bank if it considers an instruction breaches the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap. 486), or if Applicable Law requires processing other than on the Bank's instructions, unless that law prohibits telling the Bank.
watchFor: **Own-purpose licence:** a right to use 'customer data', 'usage data' or 'de-identified data' to improve services, run analytics, benchmark or train models.
**Soft deletion:** erasure 'in line with our retention policies' or 'when commercially reasonable', with no deadline, no backup rule and no certificate.

**Independent-controller wording:** terms making the Supplier an independent data user or 'controller' of account, support or telemetry data that contains Customer Data. Bank staff contact details used only to run the account are the usual exception.
**Security by policy only:** security described only as the Supplier's policy as amended from time to time. See the information security clause.

pushback.says: Our global data processing addendum is standard and not negotiable.
pushback.reply: We can work from your addendum if it gives us the means DPP2(3) and DPP4(2) require and no own-purpose use. Those means are a statutory must-have for us, so where it falls short we need a rider.

pushback.says: We need aggregated usage data to run and improve the service.
pushback.reply: Service data with no Customer Data or other Personal Data in it is fine. 'De-identified' customer data is no answer: de-identifying it is itself processing for your purpose, so you would not be only a data processor (DPP2(4)), and a new purpose needs prescribed consent we do not have (DPP3). Corporate customer data stays confidential anyway. We treat barring own-purpose use as a red line.

pushback.says: We cannot erase backups immediately.
pushback.reply: Understood. State the maximum backup cycle, keep backups protected and restore them only for us. If the period is justified by your backup design, that lets us meet the statutory must-have that data is not kept longer than necessary for processing (DPP2(3)).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Data Protection Officer with Head of Legal; a draft that misses a red line should not be signed and goes to the CRO, and for material outsourcing consider discussing it with the HKMA.

terms.title: Segregation and need-to-know access
terms.summary: SA-2 lists two typical safeguards the bank should have in place to protect customer data confidentiality: keeping the bank's customer data segregated or compartmentalised from the vendor's own data and its other clients' data, and giving access only to authorized vendor employees on a need basis (SA-2 2.5.2). For personal data they are also practical ways to meet the statutory DPP4(2) duty (inference).
require: **Segregation:** the bank's customer data is segregated or compartmentalised from data of the vendor and its other clients (SA-2 2.5.2).
**Need-to-know:** access only by authorized vendor employees, on a need basis (SA-2 2.5.2).
terms.cloud: In multi-tenant cloud, segregation is logical. Encryption with keys the bank controls is a common way to evidence it.

playbook.why: Segregation and need-to-know access are typical safeguards listed in SA-2 2.5.2, a non-statutory guidance note, so a deviation needs a rationale and compensating controls. They also help meet the statutory DPP4(2) duty and the confidentiality test in Digital Bank Guideline para 23, which the data processor and confidentiality clauses carry.
preferred: **Separable data:** Bank Data is logically segregated from the Supplier's and other clients' data and can be identified, retrieved and erased on its own (SA-2 2.5.2, 2.5.4).
**Need-to-know roles:** Access only for roles that need it, granted on approval, removed on leaving or change of role, and recertified at least annually (SA-2 2.5.2; TM-G-1 3.3.1).

**Privileged access:** Administrative and emergency access to systems holding Customer Data limited to what is strictly necessary, approved before use, logged and reviewed by someone independent of the user (TM-G-1 3.2.3).
**No live data in test:** No Customer Data in development or test environments unless de-sensitised and approved by the Bank (TM-G-1 4.2.4).
fallback: **Shared platform:** Accept multi-tenant hosting with logical segregation only, if Bank Data is separable and encrypted and tenant isolation is covered by independent assurance reports.
**Roles, not names:** Accept a list of roles and headcount instead of names, if names and access logs are available on request to the Bank, its auditors and the Regulator.
**Support from outside Hong Kong:** Accept access by support staff outside Hong Kong, only if it is role-based, time-limited and logged, and the conditions of the location clause are met.

**Break-glass access:** Accept emergency access without the Bank's prior approval, only if the Supplier approves it internally, and it is logged, time-limited, notified to the Bank [by the next Business Day] and reviewed afterwards (TM-G-1 3.2.3, 4.3.2).
redLines: **Identifiable and separable:** Do not accept Bank Data that cannot be identified and separated from other data; the Bank then cannot retrieve or destroy customer data at exit (SA-2 2.5.4) or control retention (PDPO DPP2(3)).
**Access limited by need:** Do not accept open access by Supplier personnel or affiliates 'as needed to provide the services' without approval, logging and removal rules (SA-2 2.5.2; TM-G-1 3.3.1).
model: (a) The Supplier shall keep Bank Data logically segregated from the data of the Supplier and of its other clients, so that Bank Data can at all times be identified, retrieved, returned and erased separately, except that backup copies shall be erased within the maximum backup cycle in clause [Personal data]. [For Critical Services, the Supplier shall use dedicated [database instances] [encryption keys controlled by the Bank] for Bank Data.]

(b) The Supplier shall allow access to Bank Data only to its personnel and Subcontractor personnel whose access has been approved under a documented access-management procedure [agreed with the Bank] and who need that access to perform the Services, and only to the extent they need it.

(c) Privileged or administrative access to systems holding Bank Data requires the Supplier's prior documented approval [and, for production Customer Data, the Bank's approval], shall be granted only for as long as it is needed, and shall be logged and reviewed by a person independent of the user. Emergency access granted without the Bank's prior approval shall be notified to the Bank [by the next Business Day].

(d) The Supplier shall remove a person's access rights [within [24] hours] after that person leaves or no longer needs them, recertify all access rights to Bank Data at least [annually] and privileged access rights at least [quarterly], and on request give the Bank a current list of the roles [and names] of persons with access, together with the relevant access logs.

(e) The Supplier shall not use Customer Data in any development, testing or training environment unless the data has been de-sensitised so that it discloses no personal or sensitive information and the Bank has given prior written approval.
watchFor: **Commingling:** a right to store or process Bank Data with other data 'in any manner the Supplier considers appropriate', with no promise that it can be separated.
**Open access:** support or engineering access by any Supplier affiliate worldwide 'as needed', with no approval, logging or removal rules. See the location clause for offshore access.
**Platform-wide deletion only:** Bank Data erased only when the whole platform's retention cycle runs, not on the Bank's instruction, other than backups overwritten within a stated maximum cycle.
**Test copies:** a right to copy production data into test, staging or analytics environments.

pushback.says: Our platform is multi-tenant; dedicated infrastructure costs extra.
pushback.reply: We are not asking for dedicated hardware. SA-2 2.5.2 speaks of segregation or compartmentalisation; logical separation is enough if our data can be identified, retrieved and erased on its own and you can evidence the isolation.

pushback.says: Listing everyone with access is impractical and itself a security risk.
pushback.reply: Roles and numbers will do day to day. We need names and access logs on request, because our auditors and the HKMA may ask for them.

pushback.says: Our engineers need immediate access to fix incidents.
pushback.reply: Agreed, through break-glass access approved by your on-call manager, time-limited, logged, reported to us and reviewed afterwards, in line with the controls expected for emergency IDs (TM-G-1 3.2.3).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the CISO with Head of Legal for any deviation, recorded with its compensating controls; the outsourcing committee where Customer Data of a Critical Service is involved.

terms.title: Information security requirements
terms.summary: For a digital bank, the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls and that the confidentiality and integrity of customer information will not be compromised (Digital Bank Guideline para 23). TM-G-1 sets out the expected controls, and TM-E-1, a statutory guideline, adds specific ones for e-banking. The contract should turn these into specific vendor obligations that the vendor cannot lower on its own (drafting conclusion). The statutory security duty for personal data (PDPO DPP4(2)) is in the data processor clause.
require: **Adequate controls:** the MA must be satisfied that the outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls (Digital Bank Guideline para 23). Controls should be 'fit for purpose' for the bank's transactions (para 14) and regularly reviewed as technology develops (para 15). Stating them as vendor obligations is counsel's drafting.

**Bank's IT control policies:** technology service providers should have sufficient resources and expertise to comply with the substance of the bank's IT control policies (TM-G-1 7.1.1). The provider's obligations 'may include' complying with the bank's relevant IT control policies and procedures (footnote 13).

**Access control:** unique user IDs with appropriate authentication, stronger (usually multi-factor) authentication for higher-risk activities including remote access, and strict control of privileged and emergency IDs (TM-G-1 3.2.1–3.2.3, 3.5.2). Access rights granted and removed with approval, recertified periodically, and security logs reviewed promptly (3.3.1). Need-to-know limits on vendor staff are in the segregation clause.

**System, network and data protection:** baseline security for systems: secure configuration, timely patching, documented settings, and logging protected from manipulation (TM-G-1 3.4.1); malware controls (3.5.3); network access controls, segmentation and regular review of device security settings (6.2.1–6.2.3); protected media and secure disposal, with industry-accepted cryptography and sound key management (3.1.3–3.1.4).

**Physical and personnel security:** critical facilities in secure areas with entry controls and environmental protection (TM-G-1 3.6.1–3.6.2). Third-party personnel's access to secure areas properly approved and closely monitored, and screening with verification and background checks for sensitive technology jobs, contractors included (3.6.3). Requiring the vendor to screen its own staff is an inference from 3.6.3; the people and conduct clause carries it.

**Change management:** a formal process with impact assessment, segregation so that no single person can change production without review, version control and audit trails, roll-back and post-implementation checks, and controlled emergency changes (TM-G-1 4.3.1–4.3.3). Production data used in testing only if de-sensitised and approved (4.2.4).

**Internet banking:** for Internet banking systems, including apps, strong encryption for customer information sent over external networks and for highly sensitive data such as login credentials, integrity checks, a secure Internet infrastructure with intrusion detection and patch management, application security, threat monitoring and periodic vulnerability assessment (TM-E-1 5.1.1–5.1.2, 5.2.1, 5.3.1, 5.4.1–5.4.3). Other e-banking channels, such as phone banking, self-service terminals and contactless mobile payments, have their own controls (TM-E-1 7.1–7.5). Where a vendor runs these systems, the bank can meet these controls only through the contract (inference).

**Critical operations:** an ICT policy covering cyber security, and arrangements for the confidentiality, integrity and availability of critical information assets (OR-2 6.2). OR-2 6.3 points back to TM-G-1 and the Cyber Resilience Assessment Framework 2.0 (not supplied; check).

sources.label: Digital Bank Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.16(10) of the Banking Ordinance, not s.7(3). Security and technology controls should be 'fit for purpose' (para 14) and regularly reviewed (para 15); the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls and that the confidentiality and integrity of customer information will not be compromised (para 23).

sources.label: SPM TM-E-1 E-banking
sources.note: Statutory guideline under s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance (V.4, 25 October 2024); applies to e-banking services. Section 5 covers system and network security for Internet banking only; section 7 covers other channels. 3.3.1(i): material-risk issues from the pre-launch independent assessment must be resolved, or accepted by senior management with justification, before launch. The assessment itself, penetration tests and code review (3.3.1–3.3.2, 5.3.2) are covered in the audit clause.

sources.label: SPM TM-G-1 Technology risk
sources.note: Non-statutory guidance note (V.1, 24 June 2003). Sections 3, 4.3 and 6.2 describe the bank's own controls; 7.1.1 and footnote 13 carry them to technology service providers. 2.3.4 sets the risk acceptance process for non-compliance with the bank's IT control policies.

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Final module V.1 (31 May 2022). The ICT and cyber security component of 6.2 applies to risks to critical operations delivery.

sources.label: SPM SA-2 Outsourcing
sources.note: Controls and proper safeguards to protect the integrity and confidentiality of customer information.

drafting: **Schedule, not adjectives:** put the controls in a security schedule with measurable items, such as patch deadlines by severity, where multi-factor authentication applies and the encryption standard. 'Industry standard' on its own is not enough (counsel's drafting).

**Moving policies:** if the vendor is bound to the bank's IT control policies, fix the version notified at signing and bring later updates in through the change control clause, which also deals with any cost.

**Neighbouring clauses:** testing, code review, assessment rights and remediation of findings are in the audit clause; incident reporting in the incident clause; need-to-know and privileged access in the segregation clause; staff screening and secure-area entry in the people and conduct clause; personal-data security in the data processor clause; flow-downs for a designated CI operator in the Cap. 653 clause.
terms.cloud: Cloud security is usually shared between provider and customer (a practice observation, not from the sources). Allocate each control in the security schedule to the provider or the bank, with unallocated controls defaulting to the provider (counsel's drafting), and check that the provider's assurance reports cover the services and regions the bank uses.

playbook.why: For a digital bank the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls and that customer information keeps its confidentiality and integrity (Digital Bank Guideline para 23, a statutory guideline). TM-E-1, also statutory, adds e-banking controls; TM-G-1's detailed controls are expected rather than mandatory.
preferred: **Defined security schedule:** The Supplier commits to a schedule of measurable controls for access, encryption, system and network security, physical and personnel security and change management, mapped to TM-G-1 sections 3, 4.3 and 6.2.

**Bank's IT policies:** The Supplier complies with the Bank's relevant IT control policies and procedures notified at signing or later through change control, and confirms it has the resources and expertise to do so (TM-G-1 7.1.1, footnote 13).

**Internet banking controls:** For Services supporting the Bank's Internet banking, including its apps, the Supplier delivers the TM-E-1 section 5 controls on its side, including strong encryption, patch management, threat monitoring and periodic vulnerability assessment (TM-E-1 5.1.1–5.4.3). Other e-banking channels follow TM-E-1 section 7.

**Keep pace, never lower:** The Supplier reviews controls at least annually and when threats change, upgrades weakened encryption (TM-E-1 5.1.1; Digital Bank Guideline para 15), and cannot reduce overall protection without the Bank's consent.
fallback: **Supplier's own programme:** Accept the Supplier's programme instead of the Bank's policies, only if the Bank has mapped it against its IT control policies, TM-G-1 and TM-E-1. Policy gaps may be closed or formally accepted (TM-G-1 2.3.4); TM-E-1 gaps must be closed or accepted under TM-E-1 3.3.1(i).

**Certification as evidence:** Accept a recognised certification such as [ISO/IEC 27001] and independent assurance reports as routine evidence, if they cover the Services and locations used (market practice). Direct testing and HKMA rights stay in the audit and HKMA access clauses.

**Notified changes:** Accept a Supplier right to change controls, only if no change reduces overall protection, material changes get [30] days' notice, and the Bank may object or terminate without penalty.

**Dated remediation:** Accept known gaps only under a dated remediation plan with interim compensating controls and senior-management risk acceptance. For e-banking, material-risk issues found by the pre-launch independent assessment must be resolved, or accepted with justification and periodically re-evaluated, before launch (TM-E-1 3.3.1(i)).
redLines: **Binding, adequate controls:** No signature where the Supplier's security duties are discretionary, undefined or 'reasonable efforts' only; the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

**Internet banking floor:** For Services supporting the Bank's Internet banking, including its apps, no signature without the TM-E-1 section 5 controls that sit with the Supplier, or a documented allocation showing the Bank delivers them itself (TM-E-1 1.4.2, 5.1–5.4). For other e-banking channels, apply that channel's TM-E-1 controls.

**No unilateral downgrade:** No clause letting the Supplier reduce security protection during the term on its own; 'remain subject to' adequate controls is a continuing test (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).
model: (a) The Supplier shall maintain and comply with a documented information security programme protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of Bank Data and the systems used for the Services. It shall meet at least [Schedule S (Security Requirements)], Applicable Law and the Bank's IT control policies notified [at signing or later under clause [Change control]], and be reviewed [at least annually] and after any material change in threats.

(b) The Supplier shall identify every user by a unique ID, use multi-factor authentication for privileged, remote and other higher-risk access, and control privileged and emergency accounts on all systems used for the Services as clause [Segregation and access] requires. It shall encrypt Bank Data in transit over external networks and at rest, with industry-accepted algorithms and sound key management [and Bank-controlled keys for Critical Services], replacing any algorithm that becomes weak.

(c) The Supplier shall configure systems securely, apply security patches [within [14] days if critical and [30] days otherwise], protect against malicious software, segment its networks, keep tamper-protected logs, monitor continuously for threats and assess vulnerabilities [at least quarterly]. [Schedule S] allocates each security control, including those Applicable Law requires for the Bank's Internet banking and other e-banking, to the Supplier or the Bank; any control not allocated is the Supplier's.

(d) The Supplier shall house systems used for Critical Services in secure facilities with entry controls and environmental protection, and restrict and regularly review access to them. Screening of Supplier Personnel, including those in sensitive technology roles, and their entry to the Bank's secure areas are governed by clause [People and conduct].

(e) The Supplier shall change systems used for the Services only through a documented process with impact assessment, approval by someone other than the implementer, version control, audit trails, tested roll-back and post-implementation checks. Emergency changes shall be logged and independently reviewed [and, where they affect Bank-dedicated systems, Bank Data or the Bank's configuration, approved by the Bank's designated contact at the time or, if impracticable, by the next Business Day].

(f) The Supplier shall not reduce the overall level of security under this clause without the Bank's prior written consent, and shall give the Bank [30] days' notice of any other material change to its security programme. It shall remedy any security weakness identified by the Bank, its auditors or the Regulator as a finding under clause [Audit and assessment].
watchFor: **Adjectives only:** security promised as 'industry standard', 'commercially reasonable' measures or the Supplier's policies 'as updated from time to time', with no schedule, no measurable controls and no limit on changes.
**Responsibility shifted to the Bank:** shared-responsibility wording that leaves every configuration and key-management duty with the Bank without saying which controls the Supplier runs.

**Security suspension:** a right to suspend the Services or the Bank's access whenever the Supplier sees a 'security risk', with no notice, no limit to the affected part and no restoration deadline. Limit it to an imminent threat, notified at once (see the termination, records and continuity clauses).

**Uncontrolled changes:** a right to push changes, including emergency fixes, to production without testing, roll-back or review afterwards (TM-G-1 4.3.1–4.3.3). See the change control clause for changes to scope or price.

pushback.says: We are certified; we will not sign up to your policies.
pushback.reply: Certification is good evidence, and we can map your controls to our policies instead of imposing ours. But the contract must state binding controls: the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations remain subject to adequate security controls (Digital Bank Guideline para 23). That is a must-have.

pushback.says: We need freedom to change controls as threats evolve.
pushback.reply: Agreed, as long as each change keeps or improves protection. We ask for notice of material changes and a right to object. Barring unilateral downgrades is a must-have, because the controls must remain adequate (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

pushback.says: TM-E-1 applies to banks, not to us.
pushback.reply: It applies to the Bank, and where your systems deliver our Internet banking, we can comply only through you. The section 5 controls on your side are therefore a must-have for those Services (TM-E-1 1.4.2).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the CISO with Head of Legal for any deviation, and the CRO with the outsourcing committee where a red line is not met; for material outsourcing consider discussing it with the HKMA.

terms.title: Supplier personnel and conduct
terms.summary: Vendor staff work inside the bank's premises, systems and customer relationships, and the bank stays answerable for them (CoBP 2.5). TM-G-1 expects approved, monitored access for third-party personnel and proper screening, including background checks, for technology staff and contractors (3.6.3). The core is non-statutory guidance; TM-E-1, a statutory guideline, adds controls where vendor staff handle customer authentication (4.1.3, 7.4.1), and the PDPO and the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance apply underneath.
require: **Access to secure areas:** third-party personnel, such as service providers' staff, enter the bank's secure areas only with proper approval, and their activities are closely monitored (TM-G-1 3.6.3).

**Screening:** proper screening procedures, including verification and background checks, especially for sensitive technology-related jobs, apply to permanent and temporary technology staff and contractors (TM-G-1 3.6.3). Requiring the vendor to screen everyone working on the services to an agreed standard extends this to vendor staff (drafting inference).

**Integrity of people with data access:** in protecting personal data, the bank must have particular regard to measures ensuring the integrity, prudence and competence of people who can access it (PDPO DPP4(1)(d)). Vetting, training and removal rights over vendor personnel are practical ways to show this (inference).

**Accountable for agents and providers:** banks should be responsible and accountable for the actions of their authorized agents and third-party service providers, and staff, especially customer-facing staff, should be properly trained and qualified (CoBP 2.5). Training and conduct duties for vendor personnel who deal with customers follow from this (drafting inference).

**Business conduct:** the bank should not enter into or continue an outsourcing that may compromise or weaken its business conduct (SA-2 1.2.2). Conduct standards and removal rights over vendor personnel are the contractual means (inference).

**Customer authentication roles (e-banking):** where vendor staff generate, reissue or reset passwords, segregation of duties should stop them being disclosed or leaked (TM-E-1 4.1.3); where they ask phone-banking challenge questions, controls should minimise the risk that they could impersonate the customer (TM-E-1 7.4.1).

**Bribery and conflicts:** the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201) binds the vendor and its personnel by law (not checked against the official text here). Vendor gift and conflict terms support the bank's own controls on conflicts of interest and on staff benefiting from advantages (CG-1 V.3 2.6.8–2.6.10; check V.4; inference). For agents' conflicts with customers, see the marketing and distribution partners clause.

sources.label: SPM TM-G-1 Technology risk
sources.note: Third-party personnel need proper approval for access to secure areas, and their activities should be closely monitored; proper screening, including verification and background checks, especially for sensitive technology jobs, applies to permanent and temporary technology staff and contractors (3.6.3). Technology service providers should have sufficient resources and expertise to comply with the substance of the bank's IT control policies, and the agreement may set out their obligations to ensure confidentiality of information obtained by their staff or agents and to comply with the bank's relevant IT control policies and procedures (7.1.1, footnote 13).

sources.label: Code of Banking Practice (Dec 2023)
sources.note: Banks should be responsible and accountable for the actions of their authorized agents and third party service providers; staff, especially customer-facing staff, should be properly trained and qualified; banks and their authorized agents should endeavour to avoid conflicts of interest (2.5). Annex I defines authorized agents. Non-statutory, but the HKMA expects compliance and monitors it (1.4).

sources.label: SPM SA-2 Outsourcing
sources.note: The bank should not enter into or continue an outsourcing that may compromise or weaken its internal controls or business conduct (1.2.2); due diligence on a provider covers its reputation, managerial skills and compatibility with the bank's corporate culture (2.3.1).

sources.label: PDPO (Cap. 486)
sources.note: All practicable steps to protect personal data, having particular regard to measures for ensuring the integrity, prudence and competence of persons with access to it. It names a factor; it does not prescribe vetting.

sources.label: SPM TM-E-1 E-banking
sources.note: Segregation of duties so that passwords generated, re-issued or reset are not disclosed or leaked (4.1.3); controls to minimise the risk that staff or service providers who ask phone-banking challenge questions could impersonate the customer (7.4.1). Relevant where vendor staff perform these roles.

sources.label: SPM CG-1 Corporate governance
sources.note: V.3 numbering (6 October 2017); check V.4. The bank should have a whistleblowing policy for its staff (2.6.7), policies to identify and prevent or manage conflicts of interest (2.6.8–2.6.9), and controls to stop directors and employees benefiting from advantages offered to them that may lead to improper or illegal behaviour (2.6.10). Written for the bank's own governance; applied to vendor terms by inference.

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Final module numbering (V.1, 31 May 2022). The bank should identify the people, processes, technology, information and facilities needed to deliver its critical operations, including interdependencies on third parties; key-personnel terms help with this (inference).

sources.label: Prevention of Bribery Ordinance (Cap. 201)
sources.note: Applies by law to the vendor and its personnel whatever the contract says. Not in the statute folder; not checked against the official text here.

drafting: **Key personnel:** for Critical Services, name key roles, control their replacement and require a handover. This supports the bank's mapping of the people behind its critical operations, including at third parties (OR-2 5.1; counsel's inference).

**Keep to this lane:** staff confidentiality undertakings sit in the confidentiality clause, need-to-know data access in the segregation clause, and technical controls and the physical security of facilities in the information security clause; this clause is the single home for vetting, conduct and removal of people, and for their entry to the bank's secure areas.

**Proportionate and lawful checks:** set screening depth by role (privileged technology access, Customer Data access, customer-facing work) and require checks only so far as lawful where the individual works; the vendor, as employer, runs and holds them (counsel's drafting).
**Speaking up:** consider letting vendor personnel raise concerns about the services through the bank's confidential whistleblowing channel (by analogy with CG-1 V.3 2.6.7; check V.4).
terms.cloud: Large cloud providers rarely vet named individuals to a bank's standard or accept removal of specific staff; they rely on their own personnel-security programme, evidenced in independent assurance reports (market practice, not from the sources). Focus on controls over privileged access to Bank Data and on those reports.

playbook.why: The core comes from TM-G-1 3.6.3 and CoBP 2.5, a non-statutory guidance note and an industry code, so departures need a documented rationale and compensating controls. Statute sits underneath: the PDPO makes the integrity of people with data access a factor in data security (DPP4(1)(d)), and the Prevention of Bribery Ordinance applies regardless of contract.
preferred: **Role-based screening:** everyone working on the services screened before starting, with identity, right-to-work, employment history and background checks scaled to the role, and stricter checks for privileged technology access or Customer Data access (TM-G-1 3.6.3; PDPO DPP4(1)(d)).

**Approved, monitored access:** entry to the bank's secure areas only with its approval and under its monitoring (TM-G-1 3.6.3), compliance with the bank's IT control policies (TM-G-1 7.1.1, footnote 13), and compliance with its conduct and site policies (counsel's drafting).

**Training and responsibility:** role-specific training before starting and at least annually, including fair treatment for customer-facing staff, with the vendor fully responsible for everyone it or its subcontractors put on the services (CoBP 2.5).

**Removal and key people:** a right to remove anyone for reasonable cause and exclude them at once, a screened replacement and handover at no cost, and named key personnel for Critical Services replaced only with the bank's consent (SA-2 1.2.2; OR-2 5.1).
fallback: **Vendor's own vetting policy:** accept the vendor's screening policy instead of the bank's standard, only if the bank has reviewed it as at least equivalent for the roles concerned and the vendor certifies compliance annually, with evidence available on audit.

**Removal for stated grounds:** accept removal limited to misconduct, security or compliance concerns and persistent poor performance, only if the bank can still exclude an individual at once from its premises, systems, Bank Data and customers pending investigation.

**Key personnel on notice:** accept replacement of key personnel on notice instead of with consent, only if replacements have equivalent skills and screening and a handover of at least [10] Business Days is funded by the vendor.

**Anti-bribery by policy:** accept the vendor's anti-bribery policy instead of detailed clause text, only if it covers advantages to the bank's staff and to public officials, requires the vendor to report breaches, and breach is a termination ground.
redLines: **Responsibility for people:** do not accept wording under which the vendor is not responsible for the acts and omissions of its own and its subcontractors' personnel; the bank is answerable for its providers (CoBP 2.5).

**Screening, secure areas and authentication roles:** no one in a sensitive technology role without screening to the agreed standard, or bank-approved compensating controls where law bars a check, and no unapproved or unmonitored access to secure areas (TM-G-1 3.6.3); where vendor staff reset credentials or ask challenge questions, segregation and anti-impersonation controls (TM-E-1 4.1.3, 7.4.1).

**Immediate exclusion:** the bank must be able to exclude any individual at once from its premises, systems, Bank Data and customers on a security, integrity or conduct concern (SA-2 1.2.2; counsel's drafting).
model: (a) In this clause, Supplier Personnel means the employees, agents and individual contractors of the Supplier and of any Subcontractor who perform any part of the Services or have access to Bank Data, the Bank's premises or systems, or the Bank's customers. The Supplier is responsible for the acts and omissions of all Supplier Personnel as if they were its own.

(b) Before anyone becomes Supplier Personnel, and periodically under [Schedule [ ] (Personnel Vetting)], the Supplier shall verify their identity, right to work and employment history, run the background checks that schedule sets for the role so far as Applicable Law permits, and keep evidence for the Bank. It shall not assign anyone who fails a check and, where law bars one, shall allow privileged or Customer Data access only under controls the Bank approves.

(c) Supplier Personnel shall comply with the Bank's conduct, security and site policies notified to the Supplier, and may enter the Bank's secure areas only with the Bank's prior approval and under its monitoring. The Supplier shall ensure that Supplier Personnel receive role-appropriate training on those policies, and for customer-facing roles on fair treatment of customers, before starting and at least [annually].

(d) Where Supplier Personnel authenticate customers or generate, reissue or reset credentials, the Supplier shall apply the segregation of duties and other controls in [Schedule [ ] (Personnel Vetting)] so that credentials are not disclosed or leaked, and to minimise the risk that anyone who asks challenge questions could use the answers to impersonate a customer.

(e) The Bank may reasonably require anyone's removal from the Services, and exclude anyone at once from its premises, systems, Bank Data and customers pending investigation; the Supplier shall comply and provide a screened replacement and handover at no cost. Key personnel named in [Schedule [ ] (Key Personnel)] for Critical Services may be replaced only with the Bank's consent, not unreasonably withheld, or on resignation, illness or dismissal, by someone equally skilled and screened.

(f) The Supplier shall not, and shall ensure that Supplier Personnel do not, offer, give, solicit or accept any advantage in connection with this Agreement in breach of Applicable Law, or give gifts or hospitality to the Bank's staff beyond limits the Bank notifies. The Supplier shall promptly disclose, and manage as the Bank reasonably requires, any conflict of interest affecting the Services, and report any breach of this paragraph to the Bank.
watchFor: **Vetting 'per our policies':** screening left to the vendor's discretion, with no role-based standard, evidence or audit right, or applied only to its employees and not to contractors, agency staff or Subcontractors' personnel (TM-G-1 3.6.3).
**Vendor-only staffing decisions:** no removal right, or a charge to the bank for replacement and knowledge transfer after a removal request.

**No-hire terms:** a non-solicitation or no-hire clause, often with a fee of several months' salary, that would stop the bank or a replacement supplier taking on vendor staff at exit; carve out exit and insourcing (compare SA-2 2.7.3).
**Conduct carved out of liability:** caps or exclusions that leave fraud, wilful misconduct or bribery by personnel without a remedy. See the liability and insurance clause.

pushback.says: Our background checks follow a global policy; we cannot run bank-specific checks.
pushback.reply: We do not need a bespoke process, only a standard we have reviewed and evidence that it is applied. TM-G-1 3.6.3 expects proper screening for sensitive technology roles, and the PDPO makes the integrity of people handling personal data part of our security duty (DPP4(1)(d)).

pushback.says: A right to remove our staff interferes with our employment relationships.
pushback.reply: We are not asking you to dismiss anyone, only to take them off our account. The Code makes us accountable for our service providers (CoBP 2.5), so we must be able to act on a security or conduct concern at once.

pushback.says: Anti-bribery law applies anyway, so a clause is unnecessary.
pushback.reply: The law applies regardless, but the clause adds a reporting duty and a termination right, and supports our own controls against staff receiving advantages (CG-1 V.3 2.6.10; check V.4).

playbook.escalate: Suggest Head of Legal with the Chief Information Security Officer and Head of Procurement sign off deviations, and that a refused red line on screening, secure-area access or exclusion goes to the CRO.

terms.title: Sub-contracting
terms.summary: Vendors pass work to their own suppliers. For technology outsourcing, TM-G-1 asks the bank to consider requiring notice of, or its approval for, significant sub-contracting, and to keep the original vendor responsible. The Code of Banking Practice bans sub-contracting outright for debt collection agencies.
require: **Notice or approval:** for technology outsourcing, TM-G-1 expects the bank to consider requiring notice of, or its approval for, significant sub-contracting (7.1.1). SA-2 does not address sub-contracting. Extending a notice-or-approval right to every material vendor, not only technology providers, is drafting advice rather than an HKMA expectation.
**Responsibility:** likewise, a provision that the original vendor stays responsible for its sub-contracted services (TM-G-1 7.1.1).

**Visibility (drafting inference):** obtain enough information about the vendor's material sub-contractors to map the third-party interdependencies behind the bank's critical operations (OR-2 5.1). The same information lets the bank use a failure in the vendor's supply chain as a severe but plausible scenario, which OR-2 4.3.1 lists as an example AIs may consider.
**Debt collection:** the contract with a debt collection agency should state that it will not sub-contract debt collection to any other third party (CoBP 46.5).

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Non-statutory guidance note; V.1, 31 May 2022 (the final module you supplied).

drafting: **Flow-down:** require sub-contractors to accept the same confidentiality, data-protection, audit and HKMA-access terms; otherwise the rights stop at the first vendor. In a material outsourcing this is the floor, since the MA must be satisfied that outsourced operations keep adequate security controls and customer confidentiality (Digital Bank Guideline para 23; PDPO DPP4(2)).

playbook.why: The floor is flow-down: within a material outsourcing, the must-have HKMA access, confidentiality and personal-data terms need to reach any Subcontractor handling Bank Data or outsourced operations (Digital Bank Guideline para 23, a statutory guideline; PDPO DPP4(2)). Consent, notice and register terms rest on non-statutory guidance (TM-G-1 7.1.1, for technology outsourcing; OR-2 5.1) and can be traded; keeping the Supplier responsible is the bank's own red line (SA-2 2.1.1).
preferred: **Consent for what matters:** the bank's prior written consent before any sub-contracting of a Critical Service, or of work under which a Subcontractor stores, processes or can access Bank Data, encrypted or not. TM-G-1 7.1.1 offers notice or approval; approval is the opening position.

**Supplier stays responsible:** the Supplier remains fully responsible for the Services and for each Subcontractor's acts and omissions as if they were its own, with no separate cap or carve-out for sub-contracted work. TM-G-1 7.1.1 asks the bank to consider such a term.

**Flow-down in writing:** before it starts, each Subcontractor is bound by terms no less protective than the agreement on confidentiality, data protection, security, Incidents, continuity, records, audit, Regulator access and exit. Otherwise the bank's rights stop at the first tier.

**Supply-chain register:** a current register of each Subcontractor behind a Critical Service or holding Bank Data, at any tier so far as known after reasonable enquiry, with role, locations and data access. It feeds the bank's mapping and scenarios (OR-2 4.3.1, 5.1) and concentration check (TM-G-1 7.1.1).
fallback: **Notice and objection:** for Subcontractors that hold or access Bank Data but support no Critical Service, accept [30] days' notice, a right to object and, if unresolved, exit from the affected Services without penalty, with a refund of prepaid charges. Only if responsibility and flow-down are unchanged.

**Pre-approved list:** accept a list of Subcontractors approved at signing, such as the infrastructure host, with additions by the consent or notice route. Only if the bank's due diligence covers each in proportion to its role and the list sits in a schedule changed only by agreement.

**Rights held through the Supplier:** where a large Subcontractor will not accept direct terms, accept that the Supplier holds equivalent rights in its own contract and exercises them for the bank. Only if the Regulator can still inspect or obtain reports (see the HKMA access clause).

**Commodity suppliers:** accept the Supplier's own terms for Subcontractors that never hold or access Bank Data, support a Critical Service or perform outsourced operations, such as couriers or office services. The responsibility clause must still apply to them.
redLines: **No release:** nothing that relieves the Supplier of responsibility for sub-contracted services, or that leaves the bank to pursue the Subcontractor instead. TM-G-1 7.1.1 asks the bank to consider such a term, and the bank stays accountable for the outsourced activity (SA-2 2.1.1).

**Must-have terms reach the Subcontractor:** in a material outsourcing, each Subcontractor holding or accessing Bank Data or performing outsourced operations is bound, directly or through the Supplier, by the HKMA access, confidentiality and personal-data terms (Digital Bank Guideline para 23), flow-down being the usual 'contractual or other means' (PDPO DPP4(2)).
**Debt collection:** an agency collecting the bank's debts may not sub-contract the collection to anyone (CoBP 46.5; see the debt collection clause).
model: (a) The Supplier shall not sub-contract any Critical Service, or any part of the Services under which a Subcontractor stores, processes or can access Bank Data (whether or not encrypted), without the Bank's prior written consent. The Subcontractors approved at the date of this Agreement are listed in [the Approved Subcontractors schedule].

(b) For any other sub-contracting, the Supplier shall give the Bank at least [30] days' written notice of the Subcontractor's identity and location, the Services concerned and any Bank Data it will hold or access. If the Bank reasonably objects within [15] Business Days and the objection is not resolved, it may terminate the affected Services, or this Agreement if they cannot be separated, without penalty and with a refund of prepaid charges.

(c) The Supplier remains fully responsible for the Services and for the acts and omissions of each Subcontractor as if they were its own. Sub-contracting does not relieve the Supplier of any obligation under this Agreement, and no limitation of the Supplier's liability applies more favourably to sub-contracted work than to work the Supplier performs itself.

(d) Before a Subcontractor begins work, the Supplier shall bind it in writing to obligations no less protective of the Bank than those in this Agreement on confidentiality, data protection, security, Incidents, business continuity, records, audit, Regulator access and exit, and shall give the Bank evidence of this on request.

(e) The Supplier shall keep a register of every Subcontractor that supports a Critical Service or holds Bank Data, at any tier so far as known to it after reasonable enquiry, recording the services it performs, the locations it uses and any Bank Data it can access. The Supplier shall give the Bank an updated copy [every [six] months] and within [10] Business Days after any change.

(f) If a Subcontractor's performance, a change in its control or a Regulator's concern makes its continued involvement inconsistent with Applicable Law or this Agreement, the Bank may require the Supplier to replace it within [60] days, or any shorter period a Regulator requires, at no extra cost to the Bank. If that is not reasonably possible, the Bank may terminate the affected Services without penalty.
watchFor: **Affiliate carve-out:** a clause letting the Supplier use its 'affiliates' freely, without consent or flow-down. Affiliates are Subcontractors under the definition and should be treated the same (see the intragroup clause).

**Deemed acceptance, empty objection:** changes posted on a web page with silence or continued use treated as acceptance, or an objection right whose only remedy is ending the whole agreement without refund. Ask for direct notice to named bank contacts and an objection right with exit and refund.
**Diluted responsibility:** wording that the Supplier is liable only for choosing Subcontractors with reasonable care, or only to the extent it recovers from them (see the liability clause).

**Supplier-defined materiality:** consent or flow-down only for Subcontractors the Supplier deems 'material', or a claim that a host of encrypted Bank Data has no 'access'. Tie the test to Critical Services and to holding or accessing Bank Data.

pushback.says: We use hundreds of sub-processors; we cannot ask your consent for each one.
pushback.reply: We can limit consent to those running a Critical Service; for others that hold or access Bank Data, notice with a right to object and exit will do, and flow-down still applies. TM-G-1 7.1.1 asks us to consider approval or notice for significant sub-contracting, and a change in who runs a material outsourcing may need discussing with the HKMA first (SA-2 1.3.2).

pushback.says: Our cloud host will not sign your terms.
pushback.reply: It does not need to sign with us. You need equivalent rights in your own contract with it, exercisable for us, and the HKMA's right to inspect or obtain reports must still work. That part is a must-have under Digital Bank Guideline para 23 (see the HKMA access clause).

pushback.says: We are responsible only for our own acts.
pushback.reply: You choose and manage the Subcontractor; we cannot. TM-G-1 7.1.1 asks us to consider a term keeping the original provider responsible for sub-contracted services, and we require it because our board stays accountable for the outsourced activity (SA-2 2.1.1).

playbook.escalate: Suggested: the Head of Legal with the head of third-party risk for deviations on consent, notice or the register; any flow-down gap or release of the Supplier's responsibility to the CRO and the outsourcing committee, which should consider discussing it with the HKMA first (SA-2 1.3.2; Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

terms.title: Changes to the services, the vendor and the law
terms.summary: A bank planning to change an outsourcing in a banking-related area, or its scope, should discuss the plans with the HKMA in advance (SA-2 1.3.2), and should review its agreements regularly to keep them in line with market standards and its business (2.4.2). The contract has to give the bank sight and control of changes before they happen, whether they come from the vendor, the bank or the law.
require: **HKMA first:** before changing an outsourcing of a banking-related area, or widening or narrowing its scope, the bank should take its plans to the HKMA and show that the major concerns in SA-2 section 2 are dealt with before going ahead (SA-2 1.3.2). Digital banks should discuss plans for material outsourcing in advance (Digital Bank Guideline para 23).

**Notice in time:** advance notice of vendor-initiated changes, long enough for the bank's own approvals and any HKMA discussion, and no implementation before the bank agrees (counsel's drafting, to make SA-2 1.3.2 workable).

**Controlled technical change:** the bank's change management should cover impact assessment, segregated approval, version control, roll-back and post-implementation checks, with formal procedures for emergency changes (TM-G-1 4.3.1, 4.3.2). The information security clause sets the vendor's technical change process; this clause covers changes to scope, terms, charges and the vendor itself.

**Reassess and remap:** the bank should regularly re-perform its risk assessment (SA-2 2.2.2), and review and where necessary update its mapping of critical operations, including third-party interdependencies, at least annually or following any material change to its operations (OR-2 5.1, 5.4). Change notices should give it the information to do so (inference).

**Resilience not weakened:** the bank should continually satisfy itself on a third party's operational resilience and should not continue an arrangement that may weaken the resilience of its critical operations (OR-2 6.2). It needs a right to refuse such a change, or to exit (inference).

**Regulatory change:** the bank should regularly (for example annually) review its outsourcing agreements and consider renegotiating them to keep pace with market standards and changes in its business strategy (SA-2 2.4.2). A right to require changes needed to comply with Applicable Law or a Regulator requirement is the practical tool (counsel's drafting).

**Who the vendor is:** an assignment, novation or change of control can alter the financial soundness, reputation and capability the bank assessed in due diligence (SA-2 2.3.1). Consent to transfers, notice of change of control and a termination right protect that assessment (counsel's drafting).

**E-banking enhancements:** for e-banking, the bank's policies should ensure a rigorous independent assessment before launching a major enhancement, covering relevant outsourced systems (TM-E-1 3.3.1). Vendor-led enhancements should not go live first (inference; see the audit clause).

sources.label: SPM OR-2 Operational resilience
sources.note: Non-statutory guidance note; V.1, 31 May 2022 (the final module you supplied). 5.4: review, and where necessary update, mapping at least annually or following any material changes to operations.

sources.label: Digital Bank Guideline
sources.note: Issued under s.16(10) of the Banking Ordinance, not s.7(3). Digital banks should discuss plans for material outsourcing with the MA in advance and demonstrate that SA-2 will be complied with.

sources.label: SPM TM-E-1 E-banking
sources.note: Statutory guideline under s.7(3) of the Banking Ordinance; applies to e-banking services.

drafting: **Two tracks:** separate contractual changes (scope, service levels, charges, locations, ownership), which need a signed change note, from operational changes to systems, which follow agreed change management (see the information security clause) with advance notice for anything touching a Critical Service.

**Lead time:** SA-2 sets no notice period. Choose one long enough for internal approval and any HKMA discussion, for example [90] days for material changes, and require the impact information the bank needs to reassess risk and update its mapping.

**Cost of regulatory change:** agree the rule up front: changes in law affecting the vendor's services generally at its own cost; requirements specific to the bank at agreed rates; no refusal on price grounds (market practice).

**Change of control:** define control at the vendor and its parent companies (for example over [50]% of votes or power to appoint the board); on a change, re-run due diligence and screening (see the AML vendor clause) and keep a termination right without charges.
terms.cloud: Cloud and SaaS terms often let the provider change features, sub-processors and terms by posting updates (market practice, not from the sources). Seek advance notice of material changes, a commitment not to reduce security, resilience, data location or regulatory access during the term, and an exit without charge if a change is unacceptable.

playbook.why: SA-2 1.3.2 (discuss changes to an outsourcing with the HKMA in advance) and OR-2 5.4 (update mapping after material changes) are non-statutory guidance; the Digital Bank Guideline, a statutory guideline, adds advance discussion of material outsourcing (para 23) but prescribes no contract terms. Still, a Supplier free to change the Services, its ownership or the counterparty unannounced would leave the bank unable to follow them.
preferred: **Written change procedure:** no change to the scope of the Services, service levels, locations or charges without a change note signed by both parties; Supplier proposals come with an impact assessment covering risk, security, resilience, Bank Data, dependencies and cost.

**Time for the HKMA:** material changes notified at least [90] days ahead and not implemented until the Bank approves, so the Bank can complete its own approvals and any advance discussion with the HKMA (SA-2 1.3.2; Digital Bank Guideline para 23). Emergency fixes follow the information security clause.

**Regulatory change:** the Bank can require any change needed to comply with Applicable Law or a Regulator requirement, implemented within the time required, at a cost set by an agreed rule; if the Supplier cannot comply, the Bank may exit without penalty.

**Transfers and control:** no assignment or novation by the Supplier without consent; advance notice of any change of control where lawful, with a Bank termination right; the Bank may assign or novate to group companies or a successor to its business, with the Supplier's consent given in advance.
fallback: **Multi-tenant releases:** on a shared platform, notice instead of approval for material changes is acceptable only if notice is at least [90] days, no change reduces the Bank's functionality, security, resilience, data location or Regulator access, and the Bank may exit the affected Services without charge, with an Exit Period.

**Change of control notified afterwards:** where advance notice is not permitted (for example by listing or disclosure rules), prompt notice afterwards is acceptable if the Bank's termination right runs for [6] months and the Supplier supports renewed due diligence.

**Shared cost of regulatory change:** charging Bank-specific regulatory changes at agreed rates is acceptable only if general changes in law are at the Supplier's cost and it cannot refuse a required change on price grounds.

**Affiliate transfer:** assignment to a Supplier affiliate on notice is acceptable if the affiliate is of equal financial standing, the Supplier guarantees performance, and nothing about the Services, Subcontractors or data location changes (see the location and sub-contracting clauses).
redLines: **Unilateral change:** do not sign where the Supplier may change a material outsourcing's Services, locations or delivery model without notice in time for the Bank to discuss it with the HKMA in advance (SA-2 1.3.2).
